name: Canonical identity registration transport, security, runtime, and browser-signup boundary
phase: Discovery and specification only; implementation and activation separately gated
purpose: Prepare generic secure browser registration using unchanged ZB. No FOOD privileges, account creation, live data access or activation in this slice.

sourceEvidence.ZB: register(input: unknown): Promise<IdentityRegistrationResult>; success {ok:true,value:{principalId}}; failures invalid-input, conflict, unavailable with fixed messages. ZB owns normalization, scalar password policy, Argon2 hashing and atomic persistence; no session. Existing tests proved isolated rollback/concurrency and login compatibility.
sourceEvidence.identityHttp: Login JSON parser accepts exactly email/password; no-store JSON responses. isSameOriginIdentityWriteRequest compares parsed incoming Origin with request URL, so it cannot establish independently configured trust for registration. Do not reuse that trust source or change login in ZC.
sourceEvidence.browser: Sesh studio uses email/password form plus fetch to existing identity login API. River OS login uses an access-key boolean and is not canonical principal login. No generic signup or generic principal-login page exists.
sourceEvidence.SITE: Installed Astro client.d.ts declares SITE; create-vite.js defines import.meta.env.SITE from settings.config.site. astro.config.mjs site is the owner-approved https://theriverkeptflowing.com. This is trusted build configuration, not incoming Host/URL.
sourceEvidence.security: No committed Turnstile, compromised-password checker/denylist, application rate limiter, or registration concurrency control found. No deployed WAF or other external controls are assumed. Existing middleware guards River OS only, not registration. Package dependencies provide @noble/hashes and platform primitives but no configured checker or limiter.

externalDocumentation.finding: Pwned Passwords range queries use first five SHA-1 hash characters; response suffix/count pairs allow local matching; Add-Padding requests padded results. This is documentation inspection only, no password query occurred.
Workers rate limiting uses configured bindings and counters per key per Cloudflare location. It is not a global exact quota or distributed concurrency lock. No such binding currently exists here.

transport.route: POST /api/identity/register, thin future Astro APIRoute, prerender=false; no route created now
transport.handler: createIdentityRegistrationRequestHandler(input) returns an async (request: Request) => Promise<Response>. Input contains registration: IdentityRegistrationService, expectedOrigin: string, compromisedPasswords: RegistrationPasswordChecker, abuseControl: RegistrationAbuseControl, acquireWorkSlot: () => (() => void) | null, and scheduleTimeout: (callback: () => void, milliseconds: number) => (() => void). The scheduler returns timer cancellation; callbacks/timers run only during submit. Define new checker/abuse/input types in the handler file. No optional allow-all dependencies.
transport.construction: Synchronous structural dependency validation only; no database, hasher, checker, limiter, generator, clock or service invocation. Missing/malformed/throwing configuration yields a handler returning fixed unavailable 503 without reading the body. No dependency internals exposed.
transport.ordering: Method -> exact Origin -> Content-Type/Content-Length policy -> abuse control -> local work-slot acquisition -> bounded body read -> duplicate-aware JSON parsing -> existing normalizeCredentialEmail and isValidRegistrationPassword precheck -> compromised check -> unchanged ZB register -> sanitized response. Release work slot in finally on every completion. There is no authentication gate: signup is unauthenticated. Do not call a resolver/session or imitate FOOD gate semantics.
transport.method: Reject non-POST before any other dependency/body call: 405, Allow: POST.
transport.origin: Route validates trusted import.meta.env.SITE as an absolute HTTP(S) URL without credentials/query/fragment, takes its .origin, then passes canonical origin to handler. Production HTTPS required. Handler requires expectedOrigin and incoming Origin to be canonical strings exactly equal to their URL.origin and to each other; reject whitespace, paths, null origin, multiple values, credentials, missing/malformed/wrong Origin with 403. Never derive trust from request URL, Host, Referer or forwarded headers. No CORS allow-origin response.
transport.localPreview: One explicit trusted SITE per build/deployment. Local HTTP localhost with exact port allowed only by separately configured local build using isolated test database/security fakes; never added to production trust. Preview uses its own reviewed HTTPS SITE and isolated identity target. Existing production SITE does not silently allow localhost or arbitrary preview hosts.
transport.contentType: Accept application/json only, case-insensitive media type, optionally one charset=UTF-8 (quoted or unquoted); reject extra parameters, non-UTF-8, multipart/form-urlencoded and missing type with 415.
transport.body: Validate present Content-Length as canonical unsigned decimal safe integer without sign/whitespace/repetition; oversized declaration 413, malformed 400. Count actual streamed Uint8Array bytes regardless of header; >8192 cancels stream and yields 413. If declared length is present require exact actual match. Reject unsupported non-identity Content-Encoding with 400. Read failure 503; missing/empty body 400. UTF-8 fatal decoder; reject BOM and malformed encoding. No request.json() unbounded buffering.
transport.json: One object with exactly email and password own string-valued keys. Reject duplicates after decoding escaped property names, prototype-sensitive keys, arrays, nested objects, extra/trailing values, malformed strings and numeric/nonstring field values. A bounded top-level JSON scanner must detect duplicates before materialization; depth maximum 1 for the root object, exactly two members, no arrays. Input remains at most 8192 bytes; field strings preserve original values. No generic FOOD JSON import. Existing helpers are conceptual precedent only; do not modify FOOD modules.
transport.validation: Reuse normalizeCredentialEmail and isValidRegistrationPassword for precheck before network/hash; do not add independent normalization or alter password. Pass original parsed email/password to ZB, which revalidates and remains domain authority. Password checker sees exact unchanged valid password; no principal/admin/status/hash/metadata accepted.
transport.csrf: Strict trusted Origin plus no permissive CORS selected; no additional CSRF token or session required for signup. Same-origin XSS remains outside this protection. Any future authentication/session behavior requires its own review.
transport.writes: Only ZB service/repository writes. No email-existence prelookup, principal creation in handler, compensating delete, automatic retry, or session creation. Uncertain response instructs user to try normal login first; never invent another account ID.

publicResults.headers: Every response: Cache-Control: no-store, Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. No cookies or auth tokens. 405 also Allow: POST; 429 Retry-After: 60.

body.message: Registration request processed. Continue to sign in.

ZBMapping.conflict: 202 identical body/headers; never reveal existing account

rate-limited.message: Registration is temporarily limited. Try again later.

publicResults.errorShape: {ok:false,error:{code,message}} with exactly selected fixed values; no input/exception/principal/hash in any response
publicResults.enumeration: Created/conflict have identical responses; ZB hashes once before persistence even for duplicates. Do not add early duplicate checks. Exact timing equalization is not claimed or selected: database/cache/network timing can differ. Abuse controls bound probing; deployment review measures both paths for gross differences, with no claim of eliminating every timing channel. A 202 acknowledgement proves neither creation nor email ownership.

compromisedPasswords.interface: RegistrationPasswordChecker.check(password: string): Promise<allowed | rejected | unavailable>; exceptions/malformed outcomes map to unavailable. Mandatory injected control, not a change to ZB or login.
compromisedPasswords.selected: Separate future Pwned Passwords k-anonymity adapter using injected fetch and Web Crypto SHA-1 solely for screening. Hash exact UTF-8 password locally, send uppercase first five hex characters only to fixed https://api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/{prefix}, GET with Add-Padding:true, no email/cookies/auth/full hash/plaintext. Compare uppercase suffix locally, count>0 rejects; padding count0 ignored. No lookup on keystrokes.
compromisedPasswords.bounds: Abort at 3000ms, response streamed maximum 1048576 bytes, HTTP200 required, fatal UTF-8 and strict 35-uppercase-hex:nonnegative-integer lines, malformed/oversized/failed response unavailable. No redirect, retry, fallback or caching of passwords/digests. No request/response logging. Inject network and timers for inert deterministic tests.
compromisedPasswords.privacy: Remote service sees password hash prefix and server network metadata/time; prefix constrains candidate passwords and is not zero-disclosure. Plaintext/full hash stay local. SHA-1 here is a lookup protocol, never credential storage; ZB still uses Argon2id.
compromisedPasswords.alternatives: Tiny hand-written denylist is insufficient compromised-password coverage; full local corpus requires distribution/storage/update design absent here. Select range service as smallest adapter, subject to separate owner approval for outbound dependency/privacy and operational verification. No live range query in discovery.
compromisedPasswords.failurePolicy: Fail closed 503 before ZB hashing/writes on timeout/unavailable/malformed result; no default allow or external-network fallback.

abuseControls.interface: RegistrationAbuseControl.check(request: Request): Promise<allowed | denied | unavailable>; no body read, email inspection, resolver or database calls; exceptions/malformed output fail closed 503. Inject trusted production adapter later, fakes only in next slice.
abuseControls.selected: Future two Cloudflare Workers rate-limit bindings: RIVER_IDENTITY_REGISTRATION_IP_LIMITER configured 5 attempts per 60 seconds, and RIVER_IDENTITY_REGISTRATION_SHARED_LIMITER configured 30 attempts per 60 seconds. Use registration:ip:{trusted-client-IP} and registration:shared respectively. Check IP then shared; denial stops further work and returns429. Missing/unavailable binding fails closed503. Binding declarations/namespaces belong to a separately reviewed configuration activation patch; no binding exists or is configured by this record.
abuseControls.keyTrust: Only server adapter in verified Cloudflare ingress may take CF-Connecting-IP; no X-Forwarded-For, request-body/email key, or arbitrary caller header accepted as trusted. Direct/local ingress uses explicit isolated test metadata only; production missing/unverifiable client metadata fails closed. Verify header provenance including same-zone worker subrequest behavior before activation. No IP/email logging or persistent application counters.
abuseControls.concurrency: Add process-local capacity of two in-flight registration operations via injected acquireWorkSlot returning idempotent release or null. Full slots -> fixed 503, release in finally. Holder spans bounded body read, checker and ZB. Stream read deadline 5000ms via injected testable abort/timer control. No waiter queue. This is per-isolate protection, not a global distributed lock/quota. Worker CPU budget and measured Argon2 throughput/memory plus edge rate controls must be verified before public deployment.
abuseControls.limitsAndApproval: Per-location counters are approximate/eventually consistent abuse mitigation, not exact globally enforced quotas. New bindings/namespaces and trusted ingress configuration need separate owner/config approval; no currently installed/deployed limiter capability is asserted. If runtime capacity cannot safely handle selected limits, STOP activation rather than bypass control.
abuseControls.Turnstile: Not currently configured; not selected for first boundary. No site key/secret/challenge field is introduced. Escalating bot abuse may justify a separate reviewed challenge slice, not silent activation now.

runtime.factory: createIdentityRegistrationRuntime(input) with injected database: IdentityRegistrationD1Database, expectedOrigin, compromisedPasswords, abuseControl, acquireWorkSlot, generatePrincipalId, now and testable body-read timing control. Success exposes only handler; failure fixed unavailable. No env/global imports in pure runtime module.
runtime.assembly: Structural validation first; then one D1IdentityRegistrationRepository, one existing Argon2idPasswordHasher, one DefaultIdentityRegistrationService and handler. Retain injected generators/clock without calling during construction. No DB probes or network/password operations. Future thin Astro route imports env, acquires only RIVER_IDENTITY_DB, uses trusted SITE, platform crypto.randomUUID wrapped with createPrincipalId and Date clock, then passes mandatory reviewed security adapters. No session-store construction, principal resolver or FOOD database.
runtime.configuration: Existing identity database binding sufficient. No identity schema migration; no FOOD/admin/origin configuration change. New limiter bindings require separate declaration/provisioning/typing review. Compromised service does not require an API secret. Local fakes never become production fallback.

browser.signupPath: /register, generic future Astro page; no owner email hardcoded/prefilled
browser.fields: Email type=email autocomplete=email required; password type=password autocomplete=new-password required, password policy explained in visible help text. Do not use HTML minlength/maxlength as authoritative scalar counts because UTF-16 semantics differ; server is authority. No confirm-password field or visibility toggle in first surface; no extra personal data.
browser.interaction: Follow existing Sesh identity JSON fetch convention: scoped submit script sends exactly {email,password} to same-origin /api/identity/register, disables submit while pending, clears password field/references after attempt, no local/session storage, analytics or echoed server body. Fixed messages via textContent in aria-live region; associated labels/error description and keyboard focus. Page must prevent default submission and must not submit secret-bearing form to a GET URL if scripts fail (safe inert form structure to be verified by browser test).
browser.login: 202 displays neutral acknowledgement with link to new generic /login page. /login uses existing /api/identity/login JSON flow; login issues canonical session through existing handler, no login source change. Do not route generic signup into River OS access-key login or Sesh creator provisioning. browser.headers: Signup/login pages no-store, Referrer-Policy:no-referrer, X-Content-Type-Options:nosniff; no indexing and exclude from sitemap in later UI patch. No third-party analytics/scripts on secret-entry pages. Current MainLayout/ReadingLayout analytics must not be reused there. Review existing app headers before adding CSP; no CSP claim without browser verification.
browser.privacy: No real passwords in Codex/chat, tests, source or telemetry. Logging excludes normalized/raw email, body, hashes/prefix/suffix, IP, tokens/cookies/session IDs. Minimal aggregate operational code counts only, no credential details. Inbox ownership unverified; no implicit administrator entitlement.

B: separately reviewed bounded Pwned Passwords adapter and trusted Cloudflare abuse/slot adapters, synthetic tests only; separate owner external-service/config approval remains required.

exports: interface PwnedPasswordsCheckerInput { readonly fetch: (input: string, init: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>; readonly subtle: Pick<SubtleCrypto, 'digest'>; readonly scheduleTimeout: (callback: () => void, milliseconds: number) => (() => void); }
passwordChecker.authority: Import RegistrationPasswordChecker as a type from ../http/principal-registration-api. Slice A calls check with the exact unchanged password string after its existing ZB policy precheck; no email, request, session or account data enters this checker. Defensive direct calls reuse isValidRegistrationPassword from ./../authentication/registration-service before digest/network; invalid input returns unavailable, not a new password policy.
passwordChecker.construction: Synchronous structural validation only: non-null non-array input and subtle object, callable fetch, subtle.digest and scheduleTimeout. Throwing getters or malformed configuration produce a checker whose check resolves unavailable with no dependency calls. Do not invoke digest, fetch or scheduler during construction. Preserve method receiver for subtle.digest. No ambient fetch/crypto/timer fallback.
passwordChecker.hash: TextEncoder UTF-8 of exact password, no normalization or trimming. Injected subtle.digest('SHA-1', bytes) must yield a 20-byte ArrayBuffer; invalid/rejected digest unavailable. Encode all 20 bytes as 40 uppercase hexadecimal characters, first 5 prefix, remaining 35 expected suffix. SHA-1 is screening protocol only; unchanged ZB uses Argon2id for storage.
passwordChecker.request: Adapter owns fixed https://api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/ plus five uppercase hex prefix. Exactly GET, headers {'Add-Padding':'true'}, credentials:'omit', redirect:'error', cache:'no-store', signal from adapter-local AbortController, no body. No configurable URL, query, API key, Authorization or Cookie header; this range endpoint requires no API key. Only prefix goes outbound; password, full hash, suffix, email never do. Do not log or emit telemetry for inputs, digests, requests, responses or failures.
passwordChecker.padding: Add-Padding:true requests response padding to reduce response-size information leakage. Zero-count suffixes are padding/non-positive findings, not compromised matches. Prefix disclosure remains real and needs separate live-use approval.
passwordChecker.boundRationale: Preserve approved 3000ms and 1MiB limits. 25000 lines and 20 count digits additionally bound parsing and avoid numeric overflow without needing exact breach totals; 1MiB already bounds total text. Timeout covers digest, fetch and full streamed response consumption, not just response headers. Race work against injected deadline so a fake/noncooperating dependency cannot keep check pending. On deadline abort and best-effort cancel reader; handle late rejection, cancel timer on every completion, never retry. Timer setup/cancellation failure returns unavailable. AbortController/TextEncoder/TextDecoder are local primitives, not ambient network dependencies.
passwordChecker.response: Require actual Response with status exactly 200 and readable body; no redirect acceptance. Count streamed Uint8Array bytes without trusting Content-Length; over limit unavailable and best-effort cancel. Fatal UTF-8; reject BOM. Accept LF or CRLF line endings and at most one terminal line ending; no other whitespace or blank lines. Require nonempty response and 1..25000 lines. Each line exactly 35 uppercase hex characters, colon, 1..20 ASCII decimal digits; counts may contain leading zeroes because the approved protocol requires nonnegative integers, not canonical domain numbers. Determine positive count by any nonzero digit, without Number coercion. Reject duplicate suffixes even with identical counts, lowercase hex, malformed counts, trailing data or extra separators. Validate entire bounded response before allowed/rejected decision; never early-allow or early-reject a partly malformed response. Exact expected suffix with positive count -> rejected; zero count -> ignored; valid response with no positive exact match -> allowed. Empty response, invalid stream chunks, decoding failure, unsupported digest, HTTP failure, network rejection, timeout, malformed/oversized response or uncertainty -> unavailable only. No error strings or count values are exposed.
tests: Known synthetic ASCII and Unicode vectors prove exact UTF-8 SHA-1, 40 uppercase hex, 5-character prefix and 35-character local suffix; unchanged password and no plaintext/full hash/suffix/email in outbound URL/headers/body.

Exact fixed endpoint/options/padding, no API key, no arbitrary endpoint or redirect, match/nonmatch/zero count, positive huge count without overflow, leading-zero counts, LF/CRLF/terminal-newline handling.
Empty/blank/malformed/duplicate suffix/lowercase/count overflow/trailing data/BOM/invalid UTF-8 responses fail closed; malformed line after matching suffix still unavailable.

HTTP non200, absent body, fetch/digest/read rejection, malformed digest, byte/line/count limits and exact boundaries, streamed oversize cancellation, timeout during digest/fetch/body including noncooperating promises, abort/timer cleanup/late rejection, no retries/logging/leakage.

Missing/null/array/noncallable/throwing dependencies fail closed, zero construction I/O, fake fetch/timers only. Contract test with Slice A handler proves rejected400/unavailable503 block registration and allowed reaches unchanged ZB service fake; original password preserved.

exports: interface RegistrationRateLimitBinding { limit(options: { key: string }): Promise<{ success: boolean }>; }
interface CloudflareRegistrationAbuseControlInput { readonly ipLimiter: RegistrationRateLimitBinding; readonly sharedLimiter: RegistrationRateLimitBinding; readonly trustedClientKey: string; }
abuseControl.authority: Import RegistrationAbuseControl as a type from ../http/principal-registration-api. check(request: Request) preserves the existing interface but deliberately does not inspect request or any headers/body/properties; key/config are trusted per-request injected construction inputs. No Slice A modification.
abuseControl.installedApiEvidence: worker-configuration.d.ts declares RateLimitOptions {key:string}, RateLimitOutcome {success:boolean}, RateLimit.limit(options:RateLimitOptions):Promise<RateLimitOutcome>. Use the local narrow structural interface above; do not import generated environment types or require full Worker env.
abuseControl.construction: Synchronous structural validation only: non-null non-array input and both binding objects with callable limit, trustedClientKey string matching ^[A-Za-z0-9:._-]{1,128}$. No trimming, normalization, default, request access, limiter consumption, network, database or session I/O. Missing/null/array/malformed/throwing dependencies yield control returning unavailable with zero limiter calls. Both required bindings are validated before either can consume quota. Preserve each binding receiver when calling limit.
abuseControl.trustedIngress: Future Slice C trusted Cloudflare server wiring, activated only after Slice D provenance review, reads CF-Connecting-IP solely where verified Cloudflare ingress guarantees its provenance, including same-zone subrequest rules. It validates and canonicalizes the actual IPv4/IPv6 value there, then passes that canonical IP text unchanged as trustedClientKey, an opaque bounded client-network identifier to this adapter. No request.cf country/location substitute. The adapter validates only the stated bounded key syntax; it cannot establish provenance or IP authenticity. Missing/unverifiable ingress means unavailable, never a shared anonymous key. Local/isolated tests inject explicit synthetic keys with fake bindings. No localhost exception or forwarded-header derivation inside adapter. Future runtime must construct per-request controls and never reuse another request's client key.

dimensions.key: Exact concatenation registration:ip: + trustedClientKey; direct key, no hashing/secret

dimensions.purpose: Shared registration attempt mitigation at a Cloudflare location
dimensions.key: Exact constant registration:shared; no client/email/password data

abuseControl.execution: For each check: await ipLimiter.limit({key:'registration:ip:' + trustedClientKey}); only success:true continues to sharedLimiter.limit({key:'registration:shared'}). Both success:true -> allowed. Either success:false -> denied and stop. Missing/malformed result, nonboolean success, throwing getter, thrown/rejected call -> unavailable and stop. No retry, fallback, body read, email inspection or database access. Transport maps denied to fixed429 and unavailable to fixed503 before slot/body/checker/ZB. Quota consumption is not rolled back on later failures.
abuseControl.emailAndPrivacy: No email-derived dimension selected; abuse executes before body parsing and receives no raw/normalized email. Existing normalizeCredentialEmail remains Slice A/ZB authority, no algorithm duplicated. Direct client-network key is operational personal data, not anonymous; do not log/store it in application counters. Namespaces prevent collision; no key hashing or additional secret introduced. Password never contributes to keys.
abuseControl.configuration: 5/60 and 30/60 are the existing ZC proposed numeric policy, preserved exactly. Adapter consumes externally configured bindings and does not configure/verify thresholds. Binding namespaces/IDs/declarations/typing/provisioning remain separate reviewed Slice D configuration work. Both dimensions mandatory; cannot silently replace each other. Per-location approximate/eventually consistent mitigation, not global quotas or distributed concurrency. Slice A local slots remain separate, no new slot implementation here.
tests: Both permit, IP deny skips shared, shared deny, independent exceptions/malformed/nonboolean/getter failures -> unavailable, correct method receiver and exact order/keys; missing either binding means zero limiter calls.
Missing/null/array/noncallable/throwing inputs and missing/invalid/oversized/whitespace key fail closed; zero construction quota/dependency calls; no normalization/default.

Adversarial Request forwarded/CF headers cannot affect injected key; body/password/email never inspected/keyed. Isolated keys/fake bindings only, no live Cloudflare. No local concurrency implementation or global-quota claims.
Contract test with Slice A handler shows denied429/unavailable503 before body/checker/ZB, both permitted continues in original order. No configuration/env acquisition or logging.

IPv6: only hex/colon/dot characters, syntactically valid IPv6 address; use platform URL IPv6-host parsing of 'http://[' + value + ']/' after character screening, require bracketed parsed IPv6 hostname, strip brackets, return lowercase WHATWG canonical compressed representation (including embedded IPv4 converted to hextets).
